jobs.occupation: Structural Engineer (all genders) - Material Testing & Structural Validation (Statiker/in)
jobs.description: Structural Engineer (all genders) - Material Testing & Structural ValidationHelp Accelerate Industrial DecarbonizationJoin exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.As our Structural Engineer – Material Testing & Structural Validation, you'll play a key role in developing the lightweight structural systems that make GlassPoint's technology reliable, safe, and scalable.Working closely with Structural, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Operations teams, you'll combine advanced engineering analysis with hands-on testing to validate innovative designs and ensure they perform under real-world conditions. From small-scale material characterization to full-scale component testing, your work will directly influence the next generation of technology. Your ImpactThe structures you validate will become part of some of the world's largest industrial solar thermal plants, helping heavy industry reduce emissions while improving energy security.You'll combine engineering theory with practical experimentation, transforming test results into optimized designs and helping GlassPoint continuously improve the performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of its technology.What You'll DoDesign & Improve Structural Systems- Analyze and optimize lightweight structural systems, components, and structural connections.- Evaluate the behavior of steel, aluminum, composite materials, and ETFE film systems.- Support the development of innovative structural concepts for industrial solar thermal applications.- Transform engineering insights into scalable, manufacturable design improvements.Lead Material & Component Testing- Plan, build, execute, and evaluate material and component tests.- Design and instrument full-scale structural testing.- Conduct small-specimen material testing to characterize material behavior.- Analyze test results and translate findings into engineering recommendations.Develop & Validate Engineering Models- Develop, calibrate, and improve nonlinear finite element (FEA) models.- Predict structural behavior using numerical simulations.- Validate simulation results through physical testing.- Continuously refine engineering models to improve design accuracy.Collaborate Across Engineering- Work closely with Structural, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Operations teams.- Support design decisions through data-driven engineering.- Contribute to solving complex structural challenges across international projects.- Share technical expertise and help drive continuous innovation.Who You AreYou're someone who enjoys solving complex engineering challenges and turning analysis into practical solutions.You combine analytical thinking with a hands-on mindset and enjoy moving between simulations, laboratory testing, and real-world engineering. You're curious, collaborative, and motivated by seeing your work become part of technologies that make a global impact.Ideally, you'll bring:- A degree in Structural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline (ideally with a background in construction, civil engineering, or automotive engineering).- Several years of experience in structural, material, or component testing.- Experience working with nonlinear material behavior and structural analysis.- Strong experience with numerical modelling and nonlinear FEA.- Hands-on experience planning and executing engineering tests.- Familiarity with sensors, instrumentation, and measurement systems.- A structured, analytical, and independent working style.- Confidence working in an international engineering environment.- Excellent English communication skills; German is an advantage.- Experience with foundation systems for solar structures, soil testing, rammed piles, ground screws, or percussion drilling is a plus.What You'll Find at GlassPoint- Real ownership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact from day one.- Exceptional colleagues from diverse disciplines who challenge, support, and learn from each other.- Complex challenges that require curiosity, collaboration, and innovation.- An international team united by a shared purpose and ambitious goals.- The adventure of helping build the future of industrial decarbonization. We value inclusion and foster a culture of belonging, welcoming team members of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, gender identity, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We have zero tolerance for discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation. GlassPoint helps heavy industry decarbonize by replacing fuel-based steam with solar thermal heat. This reduces energy costs and improves long-term energy security.  We’re a proven technology, already operating some of the world’s largest solar steam projects across sun-belt regions in oil and gas, metals, and mining.Ergänzende Informationen:Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach VereinbarungAnforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Materialwissenschaft, Konstruktion, Versuchsdurchführung und -auswertung

At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating to fundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for twoResearch Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order is transformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules and institutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes these processes as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating, reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutional arrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how such constellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce, transform, or erode.Job descriptionThe successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:- an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or- a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within a particular field, such as security, economy, or technology.Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.The doctoral researchers will:- develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;- conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;- contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;- participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;- present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;- contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.Your profile- An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis- A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies- A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)- A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods- Excellent written and spoken English- Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets- The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environmentWe offer- An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere- A varied, responsible and team-orientated job- Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)- Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases- A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces- A job ticket for public transport- Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centresApplicationThe Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system (https://jobs.mpil.de/3vrp7) available on our website by 22 November 2026.Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearly relates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendationThe documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early December in person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expenses cannot be covered.For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de (https://mailto:friedrichs@mpil.de) .

Within our Bank team, we are responsible for validating customer and supplier master data, ensuring adherence to internal Fraud Prevention requirements.- In your new role, you support the project team with day-to-day tasks such as mass changes.In addition, you are responsible for managing your own small projects from initiation through to full completion, as well as providing reports and supporting optimization projects.- The validation and preparation of new business partners form a core part of your responsibilities, along with various analyses and reports depending on requests and needs.- Besides that, you are ensuring that team knowledge, communications, and publications are kept up to date.- Lastly, you are in regular contact with various units across the BASF Group.- commercial vocational training or studies and first professional experience in the field of Master Data and working in projects- confident handling in working with SAP R/3, particularly in the FI module, as well as with MS Office- comprehensive knowledge of process flows, Business Partner master data workflow, products, customers and entity goals- strong analytical sense and an eye for details is required, goal-oriented, precise working methods and high customer orientation- fluent and convincing communication in English, further language skills are welcomeWHAT WE OFFER- Gross annual salary (full-time): 40.000 - 46.000 €, depending on qualifications and professional experience - In addition, you can expect a bonus dependent on the company's success- 30 days of paid vacation, special leave and sabbatical options- Flexible working hours so that you can organize your working and private life according to your needs- Location-independent working models with defined days of presence in Berlin and residence in Germany - here a first impression- Work mobile from other EU countries for up to six weeksHOW TO REACH US- Katarina Borisov (Talent Acquisition), Tel: +49 30 2005-59269 will be happy to answer your questions for this position. You are welcome to book an online appointment.- You can also reach our recruiting team here.- First information about our application process can be found here and in our Q&A video.

SAP ABAP Developer (m/f/d) (ENGLISCH)Your Responsibilities● Design and implement creative, innovative solutions for mapping logistics processes in theSAP system in close collaboration with our consultants team.● Take ownership of development tasks in ABAP OO as part of software implementations forclients across various industries● Analyze and resolve customer issues of varying complexityYour Profile● Solid experience in ABAP/ABAP OO development● Understanding of core processes and the ability to follow SAP systems customizing,recognizing its impact on programming● Strong communication skills in both German and Englisch● A true team player who enjoys working collaboratively on projectsWhy Join Us?● Fair and Attractive Compensation = Performance deserves recognition, and this isreflected in your salary● Hybrid Work & Home Office = Whether in the office or from home, you decide where youare most productive and how to organize your workday● Unforgettable Team Events = Team spirit is a top priority for us! Look forward to excitingactivities, relaxed after-work gatherings, and events you will remember● Career Growth & Development = We invest in your professional growth! From specializedseminars to individual training and mentoring, we support your career development.● Great Work Atmosphere = Work in an open, supportive and appreciative team wherecollaboration comes first. We value a relaxed environment where you can thrive.● Attractive Employee Discounts = Enjoy exclusive benefits, including become1, companybike leasing, Wellpass, and many more.● Dog-Friendly Workplace = Bring your dog to the office! Your four-legged friend is welcometo make your workday even more enjoyable

About usAirbus ist Pionier einer nachhaltigen Luft- und Raumfahrt für eine sichere und vereinte Welt. Das Unternehmen arbeitet ständig an Innovationen für effiziente und technologisch fortschrittliche Lösungen in den Bereichen Luft- und Raumfahrt, Verteidigung sowie vernetzte Dienstleistungen. Airbus bietet moderne und treibstoffeffiziente Verkehrsflugzeuge sowie dazugehörige Dienstleistungen an. Airbus ist auch führend in Europa im Bereich Verteidigung und Sicherheit und eines der größten Raumfahrtunternehmen der Welt. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.Job descriptionIn order to Friedrichshafen, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a Simulation & Modelling Engineer (d/f/m).The Simulation & Modelling division includes departments in the UK, France and Germany and represents a core competence for simulator development for spacecraft platforms, payloads and equipment.In the area of simulators, the department is responsible for producing the infrastructure that enables successful spacecraft avionics programs. Therefore, the department is looking for an experienced, talented and creative Simulation & Modelling Engineer (d/f/m) who is flexible, self-motivated and hardworking.Your locationAt the Airbus site in Friedrichshafen you will be working on innovation where others spend their holidays. Enjoy panoramic views of Lake Constance while having lunch in our canteen. And after work, join one of our many corporate sports groups to go running, sailing or skiing.Your benefits- Attractive salary and special payments- 30 days holidays and extra days-off for special occasions- Excellent upskilling opportunities and great development prospects- Special benefits: employer-funded pension, employee stock options, discounted car leasing, special conditions for insurances, transportation subsidy, employee benefits at cooperating companies- On-site-facilities: Kindergarten close to the site, medical officer for check-ups and other health-related services, lakeview canteen and cafeteria- Company sports and leisure activities such as sailing, diving and flight simulationYour tasks and responsibilities- Design and development of simulators and simulation models for satellite systems.- Creation of test procedures and test plans.- Implementation and execution of automatic and manual component-tests, integration-tests and system-tests.- Definition and creation of software releases.- Provide support to the simulator usersDesired skills and qualifications- Degree in computer science, software engineering or related discipline.- Experience in Simulation and Modelling.- Object Oriented analysis & design using UML (or similar)- Experience in the development of desktop tools using a client/server architecture.- Excellent verbal and written communication and presentation skills in English.- Knowledge of machine-to-machine communication protocols- Strong software development process knowledge- A good knowledge of development domains, frameworks and utilities (DevOps)- Excellent Knowledge on C++ & Java- Experience working with Unix/Linux and Windows Operating Systems- Will be positively considered experience on: SpaceWire, MilSTD 1553, ECSS PUS, CAN, Knowledge in spacecraft avionics systems, Knowledge in design of numerical and hybrid simulators design, Experience in Simulation and ModellingNot a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growthBy submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.
